findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "request_a_feature" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Sends a feature request, a data request or a correction straight to the person who builds this server — free, no account, and it reaches a real inbox. Use it wh…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "request_a_feature" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: review_intelligence · Private data: data_source_atlas, twin_cities_datasets, twin_cities_records, request_a_feature · Public sink: pricing_benchmark, request_a_feature · Destructive: business_teardown, local_visibility_audit, broker_diligence_prep, compose_report.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: review_intelligence · Private data: data_source_atlas, twin_cities_datasets, twin_cities_records, request_a_feature · Public sink: pricing_benchmark, request_a_feature · Destructive: business_teardown, local_visibility_audit, broker_diligence_prep, compose_report

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
